extracted.intended_audience: covered financial institutions (U.S. banks and broker-dealers that maintain foreign correspondent accounts), industry stakeholders, and the public submitting PRA comments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for covered financial institutions to obtain (re)certifications from foreign banks, maintain records demonstrating compliance with 31 CFR 1010.630, and FinCEN's Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) burden and cost estimates, with specific requests for public comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance that foreign bank is not a shell bank (31 CFR 1010.630(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered financial institutions must obtain assurances from the foreign bank that it is not providing banking services, directly or indirectly, to a foreign shell bank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns one hour per covered financial institution to comply with 31 CFR 1010.630(a)(1). This activity is included in the four-hour per-account annual burden estimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions for FR Y-7 filers and publicly traded foreign banks (31 CFR 1010.630(a)(2)(ii) and (iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign banks that file a Form FR Y-7 or are publicly traded (as defined) are exempt from the requirement to maintain lists of owners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The current notice does not assign an incremental recordkeeping burden to obtaining information necessary to establish an exemption for a given foreign correspondent account, nor does it parse exempted accounts out of population estimates. FinCEN requests comment on whether this assignment is consistent with market practices and, if not, information about methods, persons, and time involved in establishing that an exemption applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtain and review ownership information and U.S. agent (31 CFR 1010.630(d)(2)/(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered financial institutions must obtain and, if necessary, review ownership information from the foreign bank, including the name of an agent based in the United States who has agreed to accept service of legal process for records regarding such correspondent account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns two hours to comply with 31 CFR 1010.630(d)(2) or (d)(4) per (re)certification; this is part of the per-account four-hour annual burden (1 hour for (a)(1) + 2 hours for (d)(2)/(d)(4) + 1 hour for (e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Close accounts and prohibit reestablishment if foreign bank fails to verify (31 CFR 1010.630(d)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered financial institution must close all correspondent accounts with any foreign bank that fails to provide verification or corrected information within 90 days of the institution's inquiry. Once closed for that reason, the covered financial institution is not permitted to reestablish the account or establish any new accounts with that foreign bank.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns no incremental recordkeeping burden to compliance with 31 CFR 1010.630(d)(3) because records generated by closing an account or not opening new accounts are expected to be included in records documenting other extended due diligence activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reestablishment only upon receiving requisite (re)certification (31 CFR 1010.630(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: After an account is closed due to inability to timely obtain (re)certification or necessary information, a covered financial institution may not reestablish the account or open any new accounts with the foreign bank until the institution receives the foreign bank's requisite (re)certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN does not have separate data to estimate how often reestablishments occur but includes these (re)certifications in its overall estimate (approximately 177 (re)certifications per covered financial institution per year) and expects four hours of burden per (re)certification on average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on liability for compliant terminations (31 CFR 1010.630(d)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: 31 CFR 1010.630(d)(5) limits the liability of a covered financial institution when termination of a correspondent account is executed in compliance with 1010.630(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN expects this provision to reduce paperwork and compliance burden by reducing defensive overinvestment and better aligning private incentives with public interest. FinCEN assigns zero incremental recordkeeping burden to this component of the renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention to demonstrate compliance (31 CFR 1010.630(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered financial institutions must retain the records necessary to demonstrate compliance with 31 CFR 1010.630 for no fewer than five years after the closing of a foreign correspondent account, or longer if directed by the Secretary. Records include original documents provided by the foreign bank and either the original or a copy of any other document relied upon to satisfy regulatory requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN assigns one burden hour per foreign correspondent account for which (re)certification is undertaken in a given year. FinCEN solicits comments on the appropriateness of assigning technology costs for requesting, processing, and securely storing account-related data unique to FinCEN requirements and requests data on incremental annual costs incurred by affected covered financial institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for older information and interim guidance (31 CFR 1010.630(f)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Section (f) presents special rules to facilitate compliance with requirements to obtain information and (re)certifications, including interim guidance regarding information requested before October 28, 2002 and received on or before December 26, 2002.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN does not expect current or future recordkeeping burden to accrue in connection with information requested and/or received more than 20 years ago and is assigning a zero-burden hour estimate to this component.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-account annual PRA burden estimate (four hours) and breakdown
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN estimates the annual hourly burden per affected covered financial institution for each foreign bank for which it maintains a correspondent account is four hours. This covers: obtaining assurances the foreign bank is not a shell bank (1 hour), obtaining and reviewing ownership information and U.S. agent (2 hours), and maintaining records of documentation associated with the certification process (1 hour).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN estimates the same four-hour burden for recertifications and uses this to derive aggregate estimates (e.g., total annual PRA burden of 73,632 hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recertification frequency and per-institution/account population assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A covered financial institution is required to obtain an initial certification and a recertification once every subsequent three years from each foreign bank for which it maintains a correspondent account. FinCEN estimates approximately 104 covered financial institutions maintain at least one correspondent account and, conservatively, that each such institution maintains about 500 foreign correspondent relationships over a three-year horizon and opens approximately 10 new correspondent accounts per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These population and activity estimates are derived from publicly available sources (BIS/CPMI SWIFT data, ECB survey, World Bank, IMF) and FinCEN requests comment on the reasonableness of using 500 relationships and 10 new accounts per year as assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate annual PRA burden and cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN's estimated total annual PRA burden for all affected covered financial institutions to comply with 31 CFR 1010.630 is 73,632 hours, and the total estimated annual PRA cost is $8,835,840.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN uses a fully-loaded composite hourly wage rate of $120.07 (rounded to $120.00), derived by scaling mean wage data for selected occupational codes by a private-sector benefits factor. The cost calculation multiplies burden hours by this wage rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 1: data sources to estimate correspondent account populations and flows
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN requests public comment on additional sources of data (public, commercial, or proprietary) that would enable more precise estimates of the number of correspondent accounts covered financial institutions maintain in a given year and on sources to estimate rates of new account openings and/or closings annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sources or references that would improve FinCEN's population and flow estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 2: harmonization across OMB control numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN is working to harmonize its collective burden estimates across OMB control numbers and has modified recordkeeping burden estimates to account for implied per-institution burden associated with 31 CFR 1010.610 (OMB control number 1506–0046).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Is the current allocation across different regulatory requirements consistent with market practices in aggregate and accurate on an incremental or per-item basis? Provide actionable suggestions for improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 3: overlap between due diligence burdens (1010.630 vs 1010.610)
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN seeks data, studies, reports, or anecdotal information that would improve estimation and allocation of PRA burdens among related due diligence requirements for correspondent accounts (including 31 CFR 1010.610).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide references or information that help parse overlapping burden-generating activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 4: burden of establishing exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN did not assign incremental recordkeeping burden to establishing exemptions under 31 CFR 1010.630(a)(2)(ii) and (iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FinCEN asks whether this assignment is consistent with market practices and, if not, to provide information about methods, persons, and time involved in establishing that an exemption applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 5: identifying and responding to incorrect information
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN asks how a financial institution identifies potentially incorrect information provided by a foreign bank in its certification or recertification and what steps it takes if it suspects information is incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, comment on additional steps taken beyond a recertification request that would generate documentation or records (e.g., additional requests, notifications of account termination), and the role or level of senior management engagement in this process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 6: frequency and duration of interim verifications
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN notes interim verifications are considered uncommon and asks for information on the likelihood that an institution would need an interim verification, and how long the process takes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data or anecdotal information on frequency and timeframes for interim verifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 7: underestimation from excluding foreign banks' burdens
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN asks to what extent excluding reporting and recordkeeping burdens on foreign banks may underestimate the full PRA burden associated with this OMB control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents should indicate whether and why foreign-bank burdens should be estimated and provide supporting data where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 8: whether to revise PRA to account for foreign banks' burden
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN asks whether it should revise PRA burden estimates to account for affected foreign banks and, if so, to suggest sources or provide data to facilitate that update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide suggested data sources or methodologies to include foreign-bank burdens in PRA estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 9: accuracy of population estimates and bank characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN seeks comment on the accuracy of its population estimates (e.g., number of banks maintaining correspondent accounts) and requests submission of information about characteristics of affected U.S. banks that may affect their ability to incur reporting and recordkeeping requirements (such as size or operational constraints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should preferably include or reference the data relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 10: tracking correspondent accounts for non-BSA reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN asks whether financial institutions have processes to track correspondent accounts for foreign banks for reasons other than BSA compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide descriptions of those processes if they exist and any implications for burden estimation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 11: use of FinCEN sample certification form vs bespoke methods
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN asks whether covered financial institutions use the sample certification form provided by FinCEN for compliance and recordkeeping, or instead use bespoke forms or other methods to obtain required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information on which forms are used in practice and, on average, how long it takes to obtain and review the information provided by a foreign bank as part of certification or recertification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Comment 12: instances and costs of reestablishment after account closure
rubrics_metrics.description: FinCEN asks whether foreign banks seek to reestablish correspondent banking relationships after an account was closed due to failure to certify or recertify, how commonly this occurs, and whether there are additional costs associated with these instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide data or anecdotal evidence about frequency and associated costs of reestablishment attempts.
